role: the reader who holds the spec against itself
verdict: The spec does not yet meet one-problem-one-mechanism-one-name: its largest gap is that the release path, the merge gate and julieta's git are each described by two pages that cannot both be true (10 10.2's workflow grammar forbids what its release.yml needs; 05 5.3 states a code-owner review that 10 10.2 says was removed; the index routes every git call through a gitsafe that 05 5.1 defines for romeu only), and the one measurement the no-loss objective rests on (sbx env run -d against a changed env file) is probed nowhere.

findings.defect: The workflow grammar admits permissions of read or none only, no github.token, no secrets.<name> and no step env, while the same section's release.yml must attest (id-token and attestations write), create a release (contents write plus a token) and upload dora.json (12 12.10 reads GITHUB_TOKEN), and the page claims the file passes tools/ci workflows.
findings.scenario: The PR that adds release.yml (T088) runs tools/ci workflows: either it fails on the first write permission, or the grammar is loosened on an ask-first surface under release pressure, or the release is built by hand on a laptop and S1's evidence names a run that never produced the assets.
findings.change: In the grammar table, add a named allowance: a workflow whose file name is release.yml may set exactly id-token write, attestations write and contents write at job level, and may pass exactly GITHUB_TOKEN as ${{ github.token }} to the publish and attach steps; state in the release paragraph which steps need which scope; or move publish and attach out of the workflow and say so in S1 and 12 12.10.
findings.cost: a decision (which write scopes one workflow may hold), about twenty words in the grammar table, and a fixture in tools/ci workflows

findings.defect: S1's evidence says the attestation step signed the archives, while 05 5.4 Release signing and 10 10.2 say the attestation is not the signing credential and signing is an operator step with a credential outside GitHub; that operator signature has no mechanism, no journey step and no criterion anywhere.
findings.scenario: v1.0.0 ships with checksums and an attestation only; J1 step 2 verifies those; the operator signature that 05 5.4 fixed now is never produced, and a tag pushed by the sandbox's token yields a release indistinguishable from one the operator signed.
findings.change: Reword S1 to attested, not signed; add to 05 5.4 Release signing what is signed (checksums.txt), with what (one named tool and key format), where the signature is published and how J1 step 2 verifies it; add that verification to J1 and to the README outline of 12 12.8; add an evidence item for it under S1 or a new criterion.
findings.cost: a decision (signing tool and key), one journey step, one evidence row, about forty words

findings.defect: The index boundary routes every git call through internal/gitsafe and 10 10.7 links gitsafe into both binaries, but 05 5.1 defines the hardened environment for git subprocesses started by romeu only; julieta's clone, fetch, fast-forward, bundle and commit-tree calls run under an environment no page states, and 08 8.5's -c commit.gpgsign=false plus I18's test only make sense if julieta's git reads global config.
findings.scenario: An agent sets a repo-local core.hooksPath; julieta setup fast-forwards the default branch and the hook runs under julieta, not the dispatcher; or julieta's setup clone fails because GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null dropped the credential helper the sandbox injects; two implementers pick opposite answers and both cite the spec.
findings.change: Add to 05 5.1 one paragraph for julieta: which settings of the hardened runner it keeps (fresh env, no ambient GIT_* variables, explicit URLs and refspecs) and which it drops (global config, hooks path, credential helper) and why; name it in 04 4.3 setup and 08 8.5; make the index boundary cite 5.1 for both sides.
findings.cost: a decision and about sixty words; one table test in gitsafe for the julieta mode

findings.defect: romeu run step 3 runs sbx env run -d on an existing sandbox (J3a: starts or reattaches without re-provisioning) whose live sbxenv.yaml may hold a promoted recreate-class change (kits, workload, ports), step 7 only warns stale, and no block A probe measures what sbx does with a changed env file for an existing sandbox (A2 and A10 change secrets only).
findings.scenario: A kit bump is promoted; the operator runs romeu run; sbx re-plans the changed env file and rebuilds the sandbox; salvage, which is wired only through rm and recreate, never runs; unpushed work is lost while 00 0.1 promises that nothing sandbox-only is lost.
findings.change: Add a block A probe to 11 11.1: sbx env run -d against an existing sandbox after each recreate-class field of the env file changes, recording whether sbx recreates, applies, refuses or prompts; make run step 3 conditional on that result (refuse with an error id when a recreate-class change is live and the sandbox exists, naming romeu recreate), and cite the probe from J3.
findings.cost: one probe definition, one error id, about thirty words in 04 and 09

findings.defect: ADR 0008's Context says the forwarded SSH agent holds the signing key and a separate GitHub authentication key, and its deferred item is to stop forwarding that key, while 06 6.4 refuses git-ssh-sign unless the dedicated socket holds exactly one key and B2 checks ssh-add -L shows only it; the record describes the maintainer's present development sandbox, not a romeu-managed one, and neither it nor 05 5.4 nor the index's deferred row says which sandbox the sandbox is.
findings.scenario: A second adopter reads 05 5.4 and the deferred table as properties of romeu's sandboxes, concludes the product forwards an authentication key and lets an agent merge and tag, and declines it; or an implementer relaxes 06 6.4 to admit two keys because the ADR says two are forwarded.
findings.change: Add one sentence to 05 5.4's token row and to the two deferred rows: this describes the sandbox the product is developed in today, which romeu does not yet manage; a romeu-managed sandbox forwards one key through signing.agentSocket (06 6.4). Record the clarification in a superseding note per 12 12.5 rather than editing ADR 0008.
findings.cost: about thirty words in three places and one short superseding record

findings.defect: 05 5.3 states in the present tense, with no qualifier, that the ruleset requires the code-owner review and tools/ci pr requires an approval line, while 05 5.4, 10 10.2 item a, 12 12.4 and 12 12.9 each carry a patch sentence saying the review requirement was removed on 2026-10-08 and the approval-line check waits for T005; the spec describes the merge gate four times and the gate that exists zero times.
findings.scenario: A contributor reads 05 5.3 alone, believes an independent review exists, and merges a change to a security surface through the API from the sandbox; the ADR that every page must follow (ADR 0001 rule 8) describes the same absent gate.
findings.change: State the merge gate once, as it is (CI green plus the maintainer's working agreement), in 12 12.4; make 05 5.3, 12 12.9 and 10 10.2 item a cite it instead of restating the removed configuration; delete the patch sentences; keep the history in docs/reviews and ADR 0008.
findings.cost: a rewrite of about five paragraphs, no mechanism

findings.defect: Three places (the deferred row on re-reading the rulesets, ADR 0001 rule 5, ADR 0008 deferred item 3) say tools/ci all is offline, while 10 10.2's step table runs govulncheck inside all over the network and license from a container image, and 10 10.1's network rule lists neither.
findings.scenario: A local gate run on a machine without network fails in vulnerabilities and license and is read as a defect of the change; or a reviewer trusts the offline claim and adds a ruleset read to all because the network is already there.
findings.change: Replace all is offline with all makes two network reads, govulncheck and the reuse image pull, and nothing else; make 10 10.1's rule the one list of network users (add govulncheck, the reuse image, the workload image pull and the herdr download) and have the three places cite it.
findings.cost: about forty words and one list to maintain

findings.defect: The approve <name> row reads live sbx version and says it makes no sbx call (J11 step 5 repeats it), and its exit codes omit 3 although 01 1.4 says every command that invokes sbx exits 3 on a gate 1 mismatch.
findings.scenario: An implementer follows the Purpose cell and skips the version read; a stale toolchain promotes a candidate whose catalog digest the acknowledgement does not cover, which gate 1 exists to stop.
findings.change: Change makes no sbx call to makes no mutating sbx call; it reads sbx version for gate 1 and exits 3 on a mismatch; add 3 to the exit codes; mirror the wording in J11 step 5.
findings.cost: about fifteen words

findings.defect: I7's E test says each gate 2 change makes run, stop, salvage, rm, retire and pull exit 3 before any mutating call, but 01 1.5 step 4 compares the widening digest recomputed from the live files with the approval, and a new spec commit changes no live file until promoted, so no defined gate 2 change produces exit 3 for stop; a tampered live file is drift, exit 4.
findings.scenario: The test is written to its words, cannot be made to fail for the right reason, and is satisfied by a fixture that deletes the approval record, which proves nothing about an awaiting candidate.
findings.change: Define the gate 2 change the test means (an approval record whose digest no longer matches the live files, or a live file set with no approval) in I7 and 01 1.5 step 4, and state that an awaiting candidate does not block P commands, which 1.5 already implies.
findings.cost: about twenty-five words

findings.defect: J6 step 3 and 04 rm place the warning that the generation has no final handoff after julieta salvage --stop-agents has killed the agent, so the one actor who could still write /handoff --final is gone when the warning appears; 08 8.3 says the reader is asked at that moment without saying which moment.
findings.scenario: The operator runs romeu rm, sees the warning after the sandbox half, and the narrative of the session is lost although the salvage is complete; the warning's only purpose was to prompt step 1 of J6.
findings.change: Move the handoff check to before the sandbox half in 04 rm, 08 8.3 and J6 (after the preflight, before salvaging), and have rm on a TTY ask whether to continue without a final handoff; without a TTY, warn and continue as today.
findings.cost: a reordering, one prompt, about twenty words in three pages

findings.defect: 04 4.1 defines exit 1 as operation failed, but julieta lock --check, pin check, memory verify, spec validate --catalog and romeu doctor exit 1 to mean the check found something, so one code carries two meanings for the callers that are programs (the config repo's CI, acceptance command items).
findings.scenario: The config repo's validate.yml treats a network failure of julieta spec validate --catalog (exit 1, operation failed) as a catalog gap and a maintainer adds a bogus entry; or the reverse, a gap is read as flakiness and retried.
findings.change: Either define exit 1 in 04 4.1 as failed, or a check that found what it checks for, and list the check commands, or give check findings their own code (for example 6, findings reported) and update the five rows and 4.4.
findings.cost: a decision and five table cells; one new code if chosen

findings.defect: 04 4.1 promises --json on every read command, but julieta handoff show, memory check, lock --check, pin check and spec validate have none, while the mutating setup and salvage do because romeu calls them.
findings.scenario: The config repo's CI parses the text output of spec validate --catalog, and a wording change breaks it; the rule in 4.1 is read as untrue and ignored elsewhere.
findings.change: Reword 4.1 to --json on every command a program calls, and name them; add --json to spec validate and pin check, whose callers are CI.
findings.cost: two flags and about fifteen words

findings.defect: Memory entries, handoffs and state records use uppercase ULIDs (03 3.8, 03 3.9, 03 3.10) and the ledger lowercase Crockford for an APFS case-collision reason (13 13.3) that applies equally to memory/<dir>/entries/<ULID>.md on the same host disk; timestamps are named created/updated, createdAt/approvedAt/closedAt/acknowledgedAt/renderedAt/at/lastRun, observed/ingested and startedAt across the stores; manifestSha256 is neither a canon kind nor in 3.12's raw list.
findings.scenario: A query that joins a handoff's generation id to a ledger entry lowercases one side by hand; two memory files that differ only in case collide on APFS and one entry is silently dropped, which the Linux CI cannot show, exactly the reasoning 13 13.3 gives for the spool.
findings.change: Fix one ULID case for every store in 03 3.12 (lowercase, with 13 13.3's reason) and apply the case rule to the memory allowlist (I24); fix one timestamp naming rule in 03's opening and rename the outliers in the next format version; classify manifestSha256 in 3.12.
findings.cost: a decision, about thirty words, and a format version bump for the renamed fields

findings.defect: The vocabulary table, the one source of tools/ci vocabulary, has no row for concepts that carry several names or one name with several meanings: stale (toolchain record, recreate digest, run digest, mise.lock), session (a romeu invocation in 03 3.6 and 06 6.3, an agent session, an autonomous work session), tool (host settings tools, catalog tools, repo tools/*, host tools), product kit versus mixin (17 and 8 hits), operator versus maintainer (56 and 140 hits), host tool, promotion, drift, orphaned, compatibility check.
findings.scenario: A guide page says stale and the operator runs romeu recreate for a stale mise.lock; a contributor adds a session id to an event because 06 6.3 says session; the vocabulary gate passes both because neither word is in the table.
findings.change: Add a row per concept above with its one word and the Not phrases; rename recreate needed or stale to one; replace session in 03 3.6 and 06 6.3 with each romeu command that execs julieta; define operator and maintainer (or merge them for v1 and say so).
findings.cost: about twelve table rows and the edits the gate then demands

findings.defect: Boundary C and I30 say julieta runs only as delivered by romeu through the read-only mount and the compatibility check, while 01 1.1, 02 2.2 and 07 7.6 have julieta run in the config repo's CI from a pinned GitHub release with no compatibility check; the exception is in 1.1's table and in neither 1.3 nor 5.2.
findings.scenario: A mutate run or a reviewer judges validate.yml against I30 and either weakens the invariant's words or blocks the config repo's CI, which S4 depends on.
findings.change: Add to I30 and boundary C: in a sandbox; julieta also runs in the config repo's CI from a release pinned by version and checked by julieta pin check --workflows (02 2.2), where no romeu exists to deliver it.
findings.cost: about twenty words

findings.defect: 03 3.2 says there is no field for an env var for the sandbox on the page that defines panes[].env, and the index's telemetry deferred row relies on a pane env being exactly that.
findings.scenario: A reviewer refuses panes[].env as contradicting 3.2, or a contributor adds an sbx-level env field citing the pane precedent.
findings.change: Reword to: no field sets an env var for the sandbox as a whole or for sbx; a pane's env applies to that pane's steps only.
findings.cost: about fifteen words

findings.defect: 03's opening says every format has a version field, strict decoding and a JSON Schema in schemas/, while 13 13.7 gives only runtime-event a schema, ledger-entry/v1, ledger-view/v<n> and dora.v1 (12 12.10) have none, and 02 2.1's schema list omits them.
findings.scenario: tools/ci schema validates examples of every listed format and silently covers none of the three; a reader of 03 trusts a universal.
findings.change: Either add the three schemas to 02 2.1 and 12 12.3, or write the exception into 03's opening with its reason (the entry is a header line and bytes; the view is derived; dora.v1 is a report).
findings.cost: a decision and about twenty words, or three schema rows

findings.defect: 01 1.2, 02 2.1 and 12 12.3 hold three different inventories of generated artifacts, and 12 12.3 with ADR 0001 rule 17 has go generate write the diagrams in ARCHITECTURE.md, a hand-written page (12 12.8), which 10 10.2's generated step (each file generate writes is tracked with the bytes generate gives) and the Never bullet hand-edit a generated file cannot classify; ADR 0001 rejected injecting generated text into a hand-written page.
findings.scenario: The first ARCHITECTURE.md edit after T034 fails generated or is refused as a hand edit; implementers build the generator either way (the plan already chose linked files in question 27, which the spec does not say).
findings.change: Make 12 12.3 the one inventory and have 01 1.2 and 02 2.1 cite it; state that diagrams are generated into files of their own under docs/ that ARCHITECTURE.md links, and that a hand-written page is never a generate target.
findings.cost: about thirty words and two citations

findings.defect: The probe lifecycle is a table checked by tools/ci probes and owned by the probes module (12 12.2), while the index principle puts every lifecycle in internal/state and 12 12.8 promises its diagram generated from those tables; the promotion commit is a numbered procedure (01 1.6), not a table, and is promised as a diagram too.
findings.scenario: Two homes for one machine: the probe table in tools/ci and a copy in internal/state drift, which is what the principle's one-source rule forbids.
findings.change: Decide in 01 1.6 which lifecycles are internal/state tables (and move the probe table there, with tools/ci probes reading it) and which are procedures, and make 12 12.8 promise diagrams only for the tables.
findings.cost: a decision and about twenty words

findings.defect: Q25 sits in Open questions as decided, a third state ADR 0005 says the two tables do not have, and its exit is a plan task id (T101); two deferred rows also use plan task ids as triggers (the start of T005) or an unobservable one (the operator saying so), and the review-interval row duplicates the token-narrowing row above it.
findings.scenario: The plan is renumbered and the spec's triggers point at nothing; the index, the source of truth for the plan, depends on the plan's numbering; a row reopened by a word nobody records never reopens.
findings.change: Remove Q25 from the table now (ADR 0008 is its record) or move it to a Settled line; replace T005 with the event (the PR that lands tools/ci pr); merge the interval row into the token-narrowing row; replace the operator saying so with the event that makes review cheap (the panel or a ledger query exists).
findings.cost: three row edits

findings.defect: The memory layout allowlist (I24, 08 8.1) reserves import/ and no command reads or writes it; julieta memory import reads a file path given on the command line.
findings.scenario: An implementer invents a use for import/ (dropping JSONL files there for a later import) and the sandbox gains an unreviewed path into romeu's memory readers.
findings.change: Remove import/ from the allowlist, or write the one mechanism that uses it in 04 4.3 and 08 8.1.
findings.cost: one word removed in two places

findings.defect: The generation machine has two rows that record result lost (salvage --from-host keeps the generation open; run or rm finding the sandbox absent closes it), so one loss can produce two records; no page says what --from-host does when sbx ls shows the sandbox present, and no page says whether a bare romeu salvage <name>, after which the generation returns to open, passes --stop-agents.
findings.scenario: The operator runs salvage --from-host on an unreachable but present sandbox, then rm finds it absent later and writes a second lost record; or a bare salvage kills the agent and leaves the sandbox running with no agent, which the operator did not ask for.
findings.change: Make --from-host refuse when sbx ls shows the sandbox present (exit 2, fix hint: romeu salvage without the flag), and close the generation as closed-lost in that row, deleting the second path; state in 04 4.2 whether salvage alone stops agents (recommend: not without --stop-agents, which romeu passes only from rm and recreate).
findings.cost: two row edits and about twenty words

findings.defect: julieta pin workload and pin check (04 4.3, J9) reach a container registry and GitHub releases from inside the config project's sandbox, but the catalog's meta and base sets (03 3.5) hold no registry host, so the journey needs an egress.extra nobody writes; 07 7.4 says the github secret covers mise's api.github.com fallback without saying how an sbx secret becomes the variable mise reads.
findings.scenario: J9's agent step fails on an egress block the first time a workload is bumped; the operator adds a wildcard allow by hand, which I22 then fails in doctor.
findings.change: Add the registry hosts julieta pin needs to the meta set or to the config project's example spec in 02 2.2 with a sentence in J9; in 07 7.4 name the variable (GITHUB_TOKEN) and the sbx mechanism that sets it from the named secret, or mark it as a probe fact for B4.
findings.cost: one catalog or example row and about twenty words

findings.defect: The ledger is ingested only by romeu sync, run, salvage, retire and ledger ingest (13 13.4), the view is derived then, and julieta setup drains on run, so julieta event list never shows the current session's events and the lessons loop that 13.9 places in a session reads the state of the previous host command; romeu stop ingests nothing; no page states this latency.
findings.scenario: An agent records a note, runs julieta event list to confirm, sees nothing, and stops using the ledger; catalog gaps are found by egress blocks instead of by tool: other events.
findings.change: State the latency in 13 13.9 and 04 4.3 event list; add ingest to romeu stop (it is a P command that already touches the memory dir), and say in 13.9 that a session sees its own events after the next romeu command.
findings.cost: one ingest call added to stop and about twenty-five words

findings.defect: 00 0.5 claims every v1 feature traces to a criterion, an invariant, a journey or a named need, but the runtime ledger (13, two romeu commands and two julieta commands) and romeu pull have no row, and 09 has no journey in which the ledger is the subject.
findings.scenario: A scope reviewer or the plan cannot say what the ledger is for in the product's own terms; S7's journeys pass with the ledger broken.
findings.change: Add rows for the ledger (needed by ADR 0006, I31 to I33, the lessons loop of 12 12.7) and for pull (J4); add a short journey or a J-step in which an agent reads the previous session's failures.
findings.cost: two table rows and one journey step

findings.defect: 11's opening says block A needs no product code, while A3's Expect requires romeu and julieta checks to see every plant and ingest to skip each spool plant, and A5 records the hashes of sbxenv.yaml goldens that render, built after block A in 12 12.2, is supposed to produce.
findings.scenario: The task that writes A3's expectation cannot know which half to write; the goldens are written by hand before the renderer exists and the renderer is bent to reproduce them (the plan already does this in T019 and T037 and calls it its own addition).
findings.change: Split A3 into the mount facts (block A) and the product checks (a B3 case or a C id); say in 11.1 and 03 3.3 that the A5 goldens are written with the probe definitions and that render must reproduce them byte for byte.
findings.cost: one probe row split and about twenty words

findings.defect: ADR 0007's threat model defers two escapes until the sandbox-token question (Q25) is decided, which is the plan's deferred-decisions row whether agents push from a second account, reopened by block O1 item d; Q25 is decided (ADR 0008), the second account is declined, no such row exists in the index or the plan, and ADR 0008's inventory of texts it leaves stale omits this one and 05 5.3.
findings.scenario: A reader of ADR 0007 waits for a trigger that already fired and whose row does not exist; the two escapes (an untracked go.work, GOFLAGS -overlay) stay open with no owner.
findings.change: Add ADR 0007 and 05 5.3 to ADR 0008's inventory by a one-line superseding note, and give the two escapes a row in the index's Deferred decisions with a real trigger (the next change to .githooks/pre-push).
findings.cost: one deferred row and one superseding note

findings.defect: 12 12.9 and ADR 0002 say every merge is a merge commit because the fix marker and the release notes read a pull request's commits on main, while ADR 0004 decision 3 says a deployment's commits are read from GitHub so the result does not depend on how a merge was made; two records give opposite reasons for one rule.
findings.scenario: Someone proposes squash merges, cites ADR 0004, and the rule's only remaining reason is one sentence in ADR 0002 that ADR 0004 contradicts.
findings.change: Pick the reason (merge commits keep the commits reviewable and signed as written; the tools read GitHub) and state it once in 12 12.9; correct the ADR that has it wrong by a superseding note.
findings.cost: about twenty words

findings.defect: 06 6.2 lists per-name volumes that reattach on recreate as a point for the workload, and neither 08 8.5 nor 03 3.11 nor 04 rm says whether sbx env rm removes those volumes or whether salvage covers them, so 00 0.1's nothing sandbox-only is lost has an unmarked exception.
findings.scenario: The agent's configuration and caches live in a workload volume; romeu rm removes the sandbox and the volume with it, salvage reports complete, and the operator loses state the spec never named.
findings.change: Add a probe to A12 (what volumes the workload declares and what sbx env rm does to them) and one sentence to 08 8.5: volumes are outside salvage and survive or die with the sandbox as measured; or a 05 5.4 row if the loss is accepted.
findings.cost: one probe observation and about twenty words

findings.defect: The hygiene step forbids a tracked file named PROLOGUE.md because the user's agreement file lives outside product repositories; the user's agreement file is a concept of the operator's private process named nowhere else in the spec, and 12 12.4 repeats the rule.
findings.scenario: A second adopter reads a product CI rule it cannot understand, or removes it as noise and the maintainer's private file is committed.
findings.change: Either state the rule generically (a list of file names the product repository never holds, in tools/ci, with the denylist) and drop the explanation, or move the name into the denylist mechanism that already exists for names this repository must not contain.
findings.cost: about ten words, or one denylist entry

findings.defect: 09's preamble says J12 runs J1 steps 3 to 6; the J12 section says J1 steps 1 to 5; the plan noticed (question 26) and the spec still has both.
findings.scenario: The scenario function follows the preamble and the guide page follows the section; rule 13 passes both because the commands match either.
findings.change: Make both say steps 3 to 6 (install and download are preconditions on a second machine too, and step 6 is the gate J12 step 2 needs).
findings.cost: three words

findings.defect: Of the 22 except and unless clauses in the spec pages, four have no owner: revive's exported rule checks no doc comment in tools/ci and no decision extends it (10 10.2, ADR 0001 rule 14 says every exported identifier); mise exec is kept for tools/release gh after 10 10.2 names its missing-tool hazard (12 12.1); retire --force carries two meanings (04 4.2); the license step does not run on darwin while the index says every merge gate also runs locally.
findings.scenario: A doc comment is missing in tools/ci and rule 14 is believed enforced; a missing gh runs a program of the search path during a release; a Mac-only maintainer never runs the license gate and believes the local gates are equivalent.
findings.change: For each: state the decision (extend the rule by test, or accept and say so), run gh by the path mise which resolves like the other tools, split retire --force into --force and --yes, and add license to the deferred local-gate row as a named gap.
findings.cost: four sentences and one flag

findings.defect: The I4, I25 and I8 guards live in sbxdrv, e2e/fakesbx and render, which no ask-first glob covers, so tools/ci mutate (which runs on PRs touching a .go file on a listed path) never runs on a PR that changes only those guards; 5.3's reasons call the gates surfaces while some gate guards are off every surface.
findings.scenario: A PR weakens the sbxdrv builder that refuses --auto-approve; mutate does not run; the scheduled fuzz.yml catches it days later or not at all.
findings.change: Add internal/sbxdrv/** to the gates surface and note in 5.3 that every package holding an invariant guard tag is on a surface, with a tools/ci invariants check that says so.
findings.cost: one glob and one check clause

findings.defect: The rule that only docs/ and root Markdown may differ between the candidate's commit and the v1.0.0 tag is checked by tools/ci acceptance after the tag, which cannot be redone, and before it only by the maintainer remembering; the first principle calls a remembered mechanical step a defect, and the same pattern holds for the security log at each sitting (05 5.4).
findings.scenario: A kit fix lands between the candidate and the tag; v1.0.0 is tagged; acceptance fails afterwards and the only remedy is a new candidate, a new block B and v1.0.1.
findings.change: Add the pre-tag check to 10 10.2 as a tools/ci subcommand that release.yml runs first on an unsuffixed tag and fails the release before build (the plan's --pre-tag, made a rule); for the security log, write the carve-out into the first principle (operator steps that no mechanism can take) or name the detector.
findings.cost: one subcommand and one workflow step; about twenty words

findings.defect: The candidate machine names six states and 03 3.8 persists only awaiting; a crash between approval recorded and promotion step 1 is covered by no recovery row because recovery keys on promoting in render.json; the index says state is persisted in the project record.
findings.scenario: romeu dies after writing the approval and before render.json; the next command finds a candidate dir named by no awaiting record and deletes it as crashed, and the approval record points at a candidateId that no longer exists until the next sync re-renders it.
findings.change: State in 01 1.6 which states are persisted and that the others are transient within one command; add a recovery sentence for the approved window (an approval whose candidate dir still verifies is promoted by the next command, else the next sync re-renders).
findings.cost: about twenty-five words

postmortem: It is some months after v1.0.0. The product did not fail with a crash; it failed at the seams where two pages each kept their promise and the system kept neither. (1) The release never became a release: release.yml could not pass its own grammar (10 10.2 allows read or none permissions, no token), so the first release was built by hand, S1's evidence named a run that produced nothing, and the operator signature of 05 5.4, which nobody had specified how to verify, was the only real signature (10 10.2, S1, 05 5.4, 12 12.10, J1). (2) The sandbox recreated itself and salvage never ran: romeu run called sbx env run -d with a live env file a promoted kit bump had changed; the spec warned stale and attached; sbx rebuilt; salvage is wired only through rm and recreate; no probe had measured that path (04 4.2, J3a, 11 11.1, 00 0.1, 08 8.5). (3) julieta's git was not the hardened git: the boundary said every git call goes through gitsafe, 05 5.1 hardened romeu's only, nobody wrote julieta's environment, and a repo-local core.hooksPath set by the agent ran a hook during julieta setup (index Boundaries, 05 5.1, 04 4.3, 08 8.5, 10 10.7). (4) The merge gate was described four times and existed zero times: code-owner review stood in 05 5.3, 12 12.4, 12 12.9, ADR 0001, 0003, 0004 after it was removed; three pages carried a patch sentence, one did not, and a new contributor merged a token change through the API from the sandbox believing a review existed (05 5.3, 05 5.4, 10 10.2, 12 12.4, ADR 0008, ADR 0007). (5) The sandbox was two sandboxes: ADR 0008 measured the maintainer's development sandbox with two forwarded keys; the product forwards one; the first adopter read the sandbox can merge and tag as a property of romeu and declined it (ADR 0008, 06 6.4, 05 5.4, index Deferred decisions). (6) The ledger told the agent nothing in time: events were viewed on the next romeu run, event list inside a session showed yesterday, the agent stopped calling it and the lessons loop never started (13 13.3, 13 13.4, 13 13.9, 04 4.2). (7) Words drifted and the state machines were paper: stale meant four things, session three, tool four; the candidate states were never persisted; the probe lifecycle lived in a CI tool while the architecture page promised a generated diagram (01 1.6, 01 1.7, 04, 11 11.4, 12 12.8). What I would not say out loud: the review rounds produced a spec that patches sentences instead of rewriting them, cites plan task ids as triggers, and keeps a second list of its own defects in the plan; everyone saw the inconsistency and chose stands as written until the decision is made over fixing the page. That choice is the root cause of 1, 4 and 5.
lens_critique: This lens equates success with internal consistency, and a spec can be perfectly consistent and wrong for the developer, the host or the agent; it cannot tell a measured sbx fact from an invented one, so it accepts every probe-confirmed claim at face value. It also undervalues deliberate redundancy: two surfaces per path, a check stated twice as defence in depth, and history kept beside a current rule are sometimes the right call, and this reader scores each as two concepts for one. Finally it treats stands as written until the decision is made as a defect, when it is an honest and dated choice; the real cost is only that one of the four places lacks the date.
missing_viewpoint: The outside contributor opening a first pull request who is neither the maintainer nor an agent: the trust model (one account, approval lines typed by the author, a denylist of names they are not allowed to know, ask-first surfaces, a hook they must opt into) is written for one person plus agents, and no lens reads the spec as the person who must get a change merged from outside that pair; L10 the second adopter uses the product, L3 maintains it, neither contributes to it. A second gap is a licensing and compliance reader for GPL-3.0-only, CC0, REUSE and the quoted DORA report.
